- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak or adjust downward by 0.5–1.0 unit.
- If sentiment includes recent negative signals (e.g., -0.67 or 0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5 units for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >1.5 units above recent 5-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 units; if below, increase by 0.2–0.5 units.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 3 forecast values before final output.
- If sentiment shows “neutral” (0.33) or “mixed” (0.67/1.00 alternating), model tends to err on overconfidence; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0 unit for next 2–3 periods.
